# Before you start

RiboPilot runs its analysis inside a container: Docker on a workstation, or
Singularity (also called Apptainer) on a computing cluster. The container holds
every analysis tool, so you do not install them yourself.

RiboPilot is developed and tested on Linux. On a Mac it needs Docker Desktop;
Apple Silicon Macs run the container through emulation, which is slower. On
Windows, use WSL2 and run R inside WSL. On a cluster, use Singularity or
Apptainer (see [Running on a cluster](Clusters.html)).

What your computer needs:

- **Time.** The practice project (12 samples) took about 16 minutes on a Linux
  workstation with 16 CPU cores and 61 GB of memory. RiboPilot caps every task
  at your computer's CPUs and memory, so a small computer runs more slowly
  rather than failing.
- **Disk.** The container image is about 2.6 GB to download and 7.7 GB on
  disk. Each project also needs room for its own files: the practice project
  used 1.6 GB, mostly Nextflow's working files (0.9 GB) and the taxonomy copy
  (0.5 GB). Reference databases are small: the two built for the practice
  project took 4 MB and 16 MB.
  [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html) says where
  each of these goes, and how to move it.

# Install the tools

Install each of these once, and check it with the command beside it.

1. **Docker** (workstation). On Linux, add yourself to the `docker` group so
   Docker runs without `sudo`. On a Mac, start Docker Desktop. Check:
   `docker run hello-world`. On a cluster, use **Singularity** or
   **Apptainer** instead. Check: `singularity --version`.
2. **Java** 17 or newer. Check: `java -version`.
3. **[Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/install.html)**, a version
   from 24.10 through 25.10. Check: `nextflow -v`. If you have a newer
   Nextflow, RiboPilot runs version 25.10.6 instead, downloading it once. To set
   this yourself, add `export NXF_VER=25.10.6` to your shell profile.
4. **[R](https://www.r-project.org/)** 4.4.0 or newer. Check: `R --version`.
5. **RiboPilot**, in R:

   ```r
   install.packages("remotes")
   remotes::install_github("dmacguigan/RiboPilot")
   ```

::: {.alert .alert-info}
**Private preview.** While the RiboPilot repository is private, installing it
and downloading the practice reads need a GitHub personal access token. Put
`GITHUB_PAT=<your token>` in your `~/.Renviron` file (in R,
`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it), then restart R.
:::

RiboPilot does not ship a reference database. New projects may warn that the
default fish reference database is not reachable; that is expected. Build a
reference database for each group of samples in the app's Reference step.

# Check that it works

Run the practice project: see [Get started](RiboPilot.html). It exercises every
tool above, and the first run downloads the container image.

# Optional: an NCBI API key

An [NCBI API key](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/docs/v2/api/api-keys/) lets
RiboPilot query NCBI faster. It is free. The simplest place for it is your
`~/.Renviron` file, next to any other keys:

```
NCBI_API_KEY=<your key>
```

Restart R after you edit the file. RiboPilot then passes the key to every run
and every reference build, without writing it into the project's `.config`
file. You can instead pass it to `RiboPilot::new_project()` as `ncbi_api_key`;
it is then stored in the project's `.config` file and shows in the Nextflow
command of the run window.

Never paste your key into a screenshot, an email, or an issue.

# Upgrading RiboPilot

To upgrade, run `remotes::install_github("dmacguigan/RiboPilot")` again, then
restart R. While RiboPilot is in development its version number stays at
0.0.0.9018, so the number does not tell you whether you have the newest code:
read the [changelog](https://dmacguigan.github.io/RiboPilot/news/index.html)
instead.

What an upgrade means for your projects:

- **Existing projects are not converted.** RiboPilot does not yet update a
  project's database to a newer layout. When the changelog says the project
  database changed, make a new project with `new_project()`, in a new folder,
  from the same mapping file and reads, and go through the steps again. Keep the
  old folder until the new project is done. Reference databases in your
  reference folder are kept and reused, so the Reference step is quick.
- **The container image should match.** A project names its container image
  when you create it, in the `container = '...'` line of its `.config` file. Each
  run uses the pipeline scripts of the RiboPilot installed in R together with the
  R code and tools inside that image. When you open a project whose image is for
  another RiboPilot version, the app says "Container version does not match
  RiboPilot" and carries on: runs still work, with the image's code. An image with
  the same version number but older code is not detected, and a run with it can
  fail in its R steps.

To get the image that matches your RiboPilot:

- **Docker:** `docker pull macguigand/ribopilot:<version>`. Docker keeps an image
  it already has, so pull again when the image for your version was rebuilt.
- **Singularity:** delete the image file for that version from your image cache
  (see [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html)); the next
  run downloads it again.
- **Code newer than the published image:** build the image yourself from a copy
  of the RiboPilot source at the same commit you installed. This needs a machine
  with Docker; it does not work under Singularity/Apptainer alone. From its top
  folder, run `docker/deploy-local.sh`, which needs the `devtools` R package and
  (while the repository is private) the `gh` command, signed in; it tags the
  image `ribopilot:<version>`. Then:
    - **Docker:** change the `container` line in the project's `.config` to that
      tag, or pass it to `new_project()` as `container`. `new_project()` will
      warn that the tag "is not published on Docker Hub"; ignore that for an
      image you built yourself.
    - **Singularity/Apptainer (cluster):** on the machine with Docker, run
      `singularity build ribopilot_<version>.sif docker-daemon://ribopilot:<version>`,
      copy the `.sif` file to the cluster, and set the `container` line (or the
      `container` argument to `new_project()`) to the path of that `.sif` file.
  See the
  [docker folder's README](https://github.com/dmacguigan/RiboPilot/blob/main/docker/README.md).

Each image takes about 7.7 GB. Once no project uses an old one, remove it with
`docker image rm <image>`.
